title: Govt launches programme to assess fuel needs in food transport sector
byline: A special data collection programme has been launched by the government to identify the fuel requirements of transport service providers engaged in the wholesale food distribution sector, amid challenges stemming from the ongoing global war situation.

title: Visa violations: 76 Indonesian nationals arrested in Negombo
byline: A total of 76 Indonesian nationals were arrested today (20) for illegally residing in Sri Lanka in violation of visa regulations, during a raid carried out at a tourist hotel in the Porutota area of Negombo.

title: Trump calls NATO ’’cowards’’ over lack of support in Iran war
byline: President Donald Trump assailed NATO allies on Friday over their lack of support for ​the U.S.-Israel war against Iran, calling the longtime U.S. ‌allies ’’cowards.’’

title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
byline: Actor and martial artist Chuck Norris, known for his roles in Way Of The Dragon and Missing In Action, has died after a sudden hospitalisation.

title: Teenage daughter of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un drives tank at military drill
byline: The teenage daughter of North Korea’s leader Kim Jong-un was seen driving a tank alongside her father during a military training exercise, adding to speculation that she is being groomed as his successor.

title: Wife is not a maid’’: Indian Supreme Court to man seeking divorce over household chores
byline: Emphasising that household chores should be shared between husband and wife, Supreme Court on Friday observed that times have changed and a husband must share the burden of work.

title: President hints imminent fuel price hike
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake yesterday stressed the need to increase fuel prices due to the escalating fuel prices in the world market, saying that if prices were not increased, fuel supply by the private sector would be affected.

title: United Airlines to cut more flights as it eyes oil above $100 through 2027
byline: United Airlines,  is cutting more ​unprofitable flights over the next two quarters as it prepares for a prolonged period of high jet fuel prices due to the Iran war, ‌even as strong travel demand has allowed U.S. carriers to raise fares.

title: National security not a blanket to deny information: Appeal Court
byline: The Court of Appeal has ruled that invoking national security cannot serve as a “blanket or unreviewable justification” to deny access to information, in a significant judgement reinforcing the principles of transparency under the Right to Information Act No. 12 of 2016.

title: SriLankan Airlines’ bond exchange clears with 97% approval
byline: Sri Lanka has moved a step closer to closing a critical chapter in its external debt restructuring, with the national carrier securing near-unanimous creditor backing for its long-delayed bond workout, in a deal that signals both fiscal discipline and renewed investor alignment.

title: US lifts sanctions on some Iranian oil as gas prices soar
byline: The US has lifted sanctions on some Iranian oil, as it scrambles to contain the impact of its war in Iran on energy markets.

title: New microfinance authority law comes into force replacing 2016 Act
byline: Sri Lanka has formally brought its fragmented microfinance and money lending industry under a new regulatory umbrella, with Speaker Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne endorsing the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Bill, paving the way for its immediate implementation.

title: Amber alert issued for severe lightning in four districts
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued an Amber advisory warning of severe lightning in several parts of the country.

title: Presidential Secretariat uses over 600 vehicles: PM
byline: The Presidential Secretariat currently uses 634 vehicles, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya revealed in Parliament yesterday.

title: US lifts sanctions on some Iranian oil as gas prices soar
byline: The US has lifted sanctions on some Iranian oil, as it scrambles to contain the impact of its war in Iran on energy markets.

title: Next 48 hours crucial as doctors warn of hospital system collapse
byline: The next 48 hours have been identified as critical by health workers, including doctors, who warn that Sri Lanka’s hospital system could face severe disruption or even collapse within the coming week if urgent solutions are not implemented to address fuel and transportation issues.

title: Font size of Daily Mirror angers NPP Deputy Minister
byline: The concern from Deputy Minister of Mass Media, Kaushalya Ariyarathne, over Daily Mirror’s “big fonts” and front-page headlines, while the country tremors at the brink of a power crisis, is a glaring example of irresponsibility and vanity. The ignorance is bright, albeit not enough to keep an entire country away from probable blackouts.

title: President meets party leaders on energy crisis
byline: A meeting between Anura Kumara Dissanayake and party leaders was held yesterday afternoon (20) at Parliament to discuss pressing national concerns.

title: Iran fires 2 ballistic missiles towards US, UK military bases in Diego Garcia
byline: Iran launched two intermediate-range ballistic missiles toward Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, but neither struck the US–UK military base, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday, citing US officials.

title: Elephant calf dies after falling into trench made for laying railway signal cables
byline: A two-month-old baby elephant had fallen into a trench dug for railway signal cables at Horiwila, between Kekirawa and Habarana Railway Stations, and died despite the herd’s attempts to save it.

title: Sri Lanka, Brazil agree to boost trade to US$1 billion by 2030
byline: Sri Lanka and Brazil have agreed to significantly enhance bilateral trade, setting an ambitious target of reaching US$1 billion by 2030, following the second round of bilateral political consultations held in Colombo.

title: Fuel quotas increased under QR system
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has increased weekly fuel quotas under the National Fuel Pass QR system, effective from midnight tonight.

title: Shooting reported inside Yala National Park; suspects on the run
byline: Police have reported a shooting incident inside Yala National Park this afternoon, prompting an immediate response from wildlife and law enforcement officials.

title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer actor Nicholas Brendon dies aged 54
byline: US actor Nicholas Brendon, renowned for his starring role in the cult TV series Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died aged 54.

title: Three weeks in, Iran war escalates beyond Trump’s control
byline: President Donald Trump ends the third week of the Iran war confronting a crisis that seems to be slipping out of his hands: Global energy prices are surging, the United States stands isolated from allies and more ​troops are preparing to deploy despite his promise the war would be only a ’’short excursion.’’

title: Depot fuel shortages disrupt private bus services
byline: Sri Lanka’s already strained public transport system is facing fresh uncertainty as fuel distribution inconsistencies at depot level begin to disrupt private bus operations across the country.

title: Immigration nabs 77 overstaying foreigners in Negombo
byline: The Department of Immigration and Emigration today took 77 foreigners into custody for violating visa regulations by remaining in the country beyond their permitted stay.

title: Fuel prices increased from midnight
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation has increased fuel prices with effect from midnight today (21).
